published.fact: Architects Kimmo Lintula, Niko Sirola, Mikko Summanen (K2S Architects); completed 2012; gross area 352 m2
Facade of sawn-to-order horizontal finger-jointed spruce planks treated with pigmented transparent nanotech wax; windowless; CNC-cut glulam frame
Daylight enters through a void in the ceiling and washes down the perimeter wall
Only the chapel space is in the wooden volume; secondary spaces open to the square; entrances in two glass facades facing Narinkka square and Lasipalatsi

interpreted: Flare profile: footprint scaled about its centroid by 0.75 at ground rising quadratically to 0.985 at the wall top, rim lip reaching the measured ring
Plank course height 0.118 m, finger-joint segment lengths 2.1-4.3 m, honey tone range (procedural shader, no photo textures)
Flat grey roof membrane with a perimeter skylight ring 0.5 m wide inside the rim
Glazed entrance: 2.9 m high curved glass band under the east overhang, sector +/-55 deg centred 25 deg north of east (toward Lasipalatsi); size and exact position unverified
Ground level taken as the flat game terrain (y=0); the real Narinkka/Simonkatu levels differ
